findings.source_quote: ὁ δὲ ἐρᾶν με γυναικὸς ἀληθῶς ἀναπεισθεὶς ἔφη
findings.english_quote: Fully convinced that I truly loved a woman
findings.issue: The draft supplies both complete conviction through “Fully” and genuine love through “truly.” The Greek supplies one ἀληθῶς, which can qualify either the loving or the conviction; ἀναπεισθείς does not independently establish the added degree of completeness. This attachment uncertainty is not discussed in the notes.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “Convinced that I was truly in love with a woman” without “Fully.” Add a note preserving the alternative “truly convinced that I was in love with a woman,” explaining that the main rendering attaches ἀληθῶς to the supposed love because Appion is interpreting Clement’s affected behavior.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἅπαξ ἐπιτυχών, ἐπαυσάμην τοῦ ἔρωτος.
findings.english_quote: once I had succeeded, I stopped being in love.
findings.issue: Here “once” functions as an English temporal conjunction, meaning “after” or “when.” It does not explicitly preserve the numerical force of ἅπαξ: Appion succeeded once and then ceased being in love.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this wording with “after I had succeeded once, I stopped being in love,” or another rendering that explicitly preserves a single success. The preceding interpretation of πεισθεὶς and its modifiers is defensible and need not be replaced merely because its disclosed alternative remains possible.

findings.source_quote: Ταῦτα ἐμοὶ σοῦ μᾶλλον συγχώρει εἰδέναι.
findings.english_quote: Allow me to know these matters better than you do.
findings.issue: In modern English, “Allow me to know” reads as a request for permission rather than a demand to concede Appion’s existing superior knowledge. The lexical note correctly identifies the concessive sense of συγχώρει, but the main wording does not clearly express it.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “Grant that I know these matters better than you do” or “Concede that I know more about these matters than you do.”
